messages:
eva: FYI saw brief 503s during the canary in eu-west-1. looks tied to configmap rollout + node drain ordering. tagging for release decision before tonight's change window (22:00-23:00 CET).
	sam: ugh, details? what failed exactly?

eva: pods received SIGTERM, restarted, came up before configmap was updated in mount? stack logs show 503s from service layer complaining about missing feature flags. here's a snippet: 

```
2026-03-20T21:07:12Z service ERROR failed to load feature flags: configmap "flags-prod" not found
2026-03-20T21:07:13Z http 503 GET /api/v1/predict - upstream unavailable
```

chen: that sounds like our rolling update order allowed new pod to start reading an older empty volume mount while kubelet was still remounting. Did deploy-bot pause pod draining?

deploy-bot: canary: helm upgrade --install api-service chart/api v2.3.0 --namespace prod --atomic --wait --timeout 10m started at 2026-03-20T20:55:00Z

eva: deploy-bot shows helm v2.3.0, but the ConfigMap has v2.3 overlay keys applied slightly after helm. timing window ~20s. new pod came up, restarted, read mounted file that wasn't updated yet (mount propagation/flaky kubelet).

sam: options: 1) pin chart to v2.2.x for tonight, 2) pause canary and run a preflight job that forces ConfigMap patch before any pod restarts, 3) change drain order to update configmap first then rollout.

chen: +1 for preflight job. quick patchable plan: create a Job that kubectl apply -f configmap-patch.yaml --namespace prod and verify resourceVersion bumped, then trigger helm canary. avoids rollbacks and keeps release moving.

eva: downside: if helm includes configmap changes in chart then manual patching may cause diff noise and rollouts to re-trigger. but acceptable for a one-off hotfix.

release-coordinator: Also need release notes updated: call out that configmap overlays are handled separately and we did a preflight patch. I'll add a short bullet under "notes" and update the staging checklist.

sam: if we do preflight, test plan: 
- run job in eu-west-1 staging first 
- verify pods see updated /etc/config/flags.yaml (cat inside pod) 
- run smoke (10 req/s) for 2m 
- then run helm canary with deploy-bot via release pipeline

chen: commands for verification: 
```
# patch cm
kubectl apply -f configmap-patch.yaml -n prod
# check resourceVersion
kubectl get configmap flags-prod -n prod -o jsonpath='{.metadata.resourceVersion}'
# quick pod check
kubectl exec -n prod $(kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=api -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- cat /etc/config/flags.yaml
```

eva: alternative is to change Helm values so chart doesn't force pod restart on configmap update: set values.featureFlagsConfig.enabled=false and use external watcher. Not for tonight.

deploy-bot: suggested hold: canary auto-pause threshold breached: 503 spike >0.5% in 5m. Pausing further promotion.

sam: consensus? I'm leaning preflight + keep chart version (v2.3.0) so we don't stall other dependency upgrades.

release-coordinator: agreed. plan for tonight: 
- 21:30 run preflight patch job in prod eu-west-1 (release ops oncall: chen) 
- 21:45 verify resourceVersion + pod cat check (sam) 
- 22:00 re-run helm canary via deploy-bot (eva) 
- 22:10 smoke + rollback window until 22:30 (if >1% 5m error, rollback to v2.2.9)
- update release notes: add configmap preflight step and mention manual patch.

chen: i'll prepare configmap-patch.yaml and a small Job manifest; will run a staging test in 10m and paste links to CI run.

eva: ok please add a postmortem note to the release thread if we still see the mount glitch; may need kubelet restart/diff on node image (rare).

sam: thanks. adding checklist to the PR and tagging slack #oncall for the window. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled: canary resume at 2026-03-20T22:00:00Z if preflight tag status == success.
